title: Relying Exclusively on CLI Arguments for Complex Configs
damaged_code:
```bash
# Complex invocation coupled to transient terminal states
app --port=8080 --db-host=localhost --db-user=admin --db-pass=secret --thread-pool=32 --cache-limit=1024
```
pattern: Exposing dozens of operational parameters solely as command line flags, lacking file-system configuration schema alternatives.
why_bad: Forces operators to write complex, error-prone shell startup scripts. It makes configuration auditing impossible, as CLI arguments are transient and easily leaked in process lists (`ps aux`).
detection: The presence of extensive argument parsing maps without file-based fallback deserializers.
fix: Provide an option to supply configuration files (e.g. in YAML or TOML); limit CLI flags to bootstrap variables like the config path itself.
source: [Pragmatic Programmers] Michael T. Nygard - *Release It!_ Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software* (2007, Pragmatic Bookshelf).pdf, Section 14.2.
